caption:
TSMC CEO C.C. Wei says the chipmaker is talking with Elon Musk's Terafab project in Texas, but any fab it joins has to be run by TSMC.
Musk said last week that TSMC could sublease part of Terafab, "but nothing more than that."
The comments came as TSMC reported a 69 percent jump in quarterly profit.

Who should run Musk's giant chip plant?

Follow @neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: The Next Web, Tom's Hardware · Photo: Not a Tesla App, Spectrum News 1

slides.headline: Musk wants to run his giant chip plant himself. TSMC says *only TSMC runs the fab*

slides.heading: Wei's *one condition*
paras: On TSMC's third quarter earnings call, CEO C.C. Wei confirmed talks about working with Terafab, Elon Musk's chipmaking project in Texas.
"We are still in discussion, let me say that. But the fab has got to be run by TSMC," Wei told analysts, according to Bloomberg.

slides.heading: Musk said *nothing more*
paras: On October 7, Musk wrote on X that Tesla and SpaceX would build and run the plant themselves.
"Maybe TSMC subleases part of the Terafab if they want, but nothing more than that," he wrote. Wei said no deal has been reached and gave no timeline.

slides.heading: A plant *bigger than a town*
paras: Terafab is a Tesla, SpaceX and xAI project in Grimes County, Texas. Its first phase is a $16.8 billion fab that broke ground in August.
The campus is planned at more than 100 million square feet, with at least 3,000 jobs. Intel is expected to supply its 14A process.

slides.heading: TSMC's *record quarter*
paras: TSMC's July to September net profit rose 69 percent to NT$763.1 billion, about $23.6 billion, beating estimates. Revenue hit $46.7 billion, up 41 percent.

paras.t: TSMC expects up to $54.3 billion in revenue next quarter, and it is scouting Texas for new US capacity.

slides.hook: Follow to see who blinks first in the fight over Musk's Texas chip plant.
